# mach_msg2 (trap -47) golden capture — M2-mach Task 2
#
# Captured from a REAL, live, bounded run of the currently-blocked dynamic guest:
#
#   cargo build -p retrace
#   codesign -s - -f --entitlements retrace.entitlements target/aarch64-apple-darwin/debug/retrace
#   HD=$(find target -name hello_dyn -path "*out*" | head -1)
#   RETRACE_TRACE=1 perl -e 'alarm 60; exec @ARGV' -- \
#     ./target/aarch64-apple-darwin/debug/retrace record-dyn "$HD" -o /tmp/m2mach-capture.bin 2>capture.log
#
# Host OS (`sw_vers`):
#   ProductName:    macOS
#   ProductVersion: 26.4.1
#   BuildVersion:   25E253
#
# These are AUTHENTIC wire bytes: the guest's mach_msg2 send buffers (hexdumped from guest
# memory at args[0] before the trap is forwarded to the host kernel) and the host kernel's
# reply bytes (hexdumped from the memory-diff `writes` produced by forward_and_diff after the
# trap returns). Nothing here is transcribed from documentation or round-tripped by hand.
#
# The run reaches 6 mach_msg2 calls (msgh_id 200, 206, 3418, 4811, 4822, 4811 again) and then
# hits the known libmalloc wall this milestone is working to remove: "pointer range initial
# reservation failed" surfaces later as a BRK (EC=0x3c ISS=0x1 FSC=0x1) in libmalloc/libsystem,
# not shown here because it is not a mach_msg2 event — see capture.log tail for the abort.
#
# IMPORTANT ANNOTATION — msgh_id 4811 (_kernelrpc_mach_vm_map) reply framing:
#   rcv_size for 4811 is reported as 52, but the diff `writes` region captured here spans a
#   wider x0-window (up to 256 bytes — the RETRACE_TRACE diagnostic's fixed `.min(256)` dump
#   cap, applied over forward_and_diff's snapshot window around x0, not exactly rcv_size bytes).
#   The REPLY PROPER is only the FIRST 52 BYTES of the reply@... hexdump below: a 44-byte MIG
#   reply (mach_msg_header_t[24] + NDR[8] + retcode[4] + address-out[8] = 44) followed by an
#   8-byte mach_msg trailer (mach_msg_trailer_t, MACH_MSG_TRAILER_FORMAT_0, size=8) = 52 bytes
#   total. Bytes beyond offset +0x34 (52) in the two 4811 reply dumps below are residual bytes
#   from the guest's stack/prior request buffer content that happened to fall inside the diffed
#   window — NOT part of the kernel's actual reply. The codec must only decode the first 52 bytes.
#
# GROUND-TRUTH DECODE (offsets verified via offsetof against this SDK's mig struct; reply
# offsets Head[24]+NDR[24..32]+RetCode[32..36]+address[36..44]+trailer[44..52]). Downstream
# tasks (codec unit tests + servicing) MUST use these real values, NOT idealized guesses:
#
#   msg 4 (1st 4811): REQ address=0x0  size=0x4a0000  mask=0  flags=0x01000001 (ANYWHERE|0x01000000)
#                         cur_prot=0 (PROT_NONE, i.e. an address-space RESERVATION) max_prot=0 inherit=1
#                     REPLY RetCode=0 (KERN_SUCCESS) address=0x109674000  <-- a HOST address in
#                         retrace's OWN space (~4.15 GiB); libmalloc wanted it in the guest nano
#                         band and rejects it. This is the M2c-6 "out-of-nano-range" failure.
#   msg 6 (2nd 4811): REQ address=0x400000000  size=0x600000000 (24 GiB!)  mask=0  flags=0x0 (FIXED)
#                         cur_prot=0 (PROT_NONE reservation) max_prot=0 inherit=1
#                     REPLY RetCode=3 (KERN_NO_SPACE) address=0x800000000  <-- the FIXED 24 GiB
#                         reservation could not be placed in retrace's host space.
#
#   SERVICING IMPLICATIONS (for Tasks 5/7, flagged here so they aren't a surprise):
#   - Both 4811s are PROT_NONE reservations, not backed allocations. cur_protection=0.
#   - msg 4 is ANYWHERE (flags&1=1); msg 6 is FIXED (flags&1=0) at 0x400000000. The two are NOT
#     interchangeable — a decoder/servicing test must cover both shapes.
#   - msg 6 requests a 24 GiB region. Naively backing it (alloc_pages(0x600000000) + hv_vm_map of
#     24 GiB) is the open servicing risk: it may exceed host/hv limits, and guest stage-1 identity
#     coverage of IPA 0x4_0000_0000..0xA_0000_0000 is unverified. The empirical walk (Task 7) is
#     where this resolves; Task 5 only needs the FIRST serviceable 4811 to move the wall.
#
# Routine names (msgh_id -> name), from Mach kernel MIG subsystem numbering:
#   200  = host_info
#   206  = host_get_clock_service
#   3418 = semaphore_create (task subsystem base 3400 + selector 18)
#   4811 = _kernelrpc_mach_vm_map (mach_vm subsystem base 4800 + selector 11)
#   4822 = mach_vm_deferred_reclamation_buffer_allocate (mach_vm subsystem base 4800 + selector 22)
#
# ============================================================================

# non-mach_msg2 traps (-12 mach_vm_deallocate, -15 mach_vm_protect, -89, etc.)
# and hits the known libmalloc "pointer range initial reservation failed"
# wall this milestone is working to clear, surfacing as:
#
#   RECORD ERROR: non-syscall exit: exception (EC=0x3c ISS=0x1 FSC=0x1) far/ipa=0x0 (UNMAPPED) pc=0x4404 elr=0x180322818

# This is the EXPECTED, correct outcome for this capture run.
